The *Kumārakassapattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 537) is a biographical verse text preserved in the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. It recounts the past-life deeds and spiritual trajectory of the elder Kumāra Kassapa. According to SuttaCentral metadata, the text is referenced in connection with the *Nigrodhamigajātaka* (Ja 12) and the *Nigrodhajātaka* (Ja 445), and has five modern translations across five languages [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal parallels, registering 188 matching passages across 33 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial reuse occurs in the commentarial literature, prominently the first volume of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (matching segments §1.1–25.4), the second volume of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In addition, formulaic biographical and devotional verses are widely shared with other *Therāpadāna* and *Therīapadāna* texts, including the *Sīvalittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 545), *Mahākoṭṭhikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 539), *Uruveḷakassapattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 540), and *Soṇātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 26) [DharmaNexus]. Outside the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus records weak machine alignments with Kṣemendra's Tibetan *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155-2) and the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26, fascicle 39) [DharmaNexus].
